newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: DBS Land to raise A$149.88 mln from float.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land to raise A$149.88 mln from float.

text.p: Singapore property and hotel company DBS Land Ltd said on Monday that it would raise A$149.88 million from the offer of shares in its Australian property development group Australand Holdings Ltd.
DBS said Australand would be listed on the Australian and Singapore stock exchanges, with trading due to begin on June 16.

It said 48 million shares would be offered to Australian investors at A$1.20 each, DBS itself would acquire another 48 million shares at the same price, and Singapore institutions and public would be offered 28.9 million shares at A$1.20 each.
In all, existing Australand shareholders would own 73.5 percent of the company with 16.5 percent held by Australian investors and 10 percent stake held by Singapore institutions.
SBC Warburg would underwrite the Australian issue.

The prospectus forecast 1997 net profit of A$27.8 million, just above the 1996 result of A$27.5 million, but rising sharply to A$48.1 million in 1998. The profit rise was based on a surge in expected revenue to A$433.1 million next year from A$272.6 million this year and A$209.7 million in 1996.
The expected 1997 dividend yield was 5.3 percent, rising to 7.5 percent next year.
DBS said Australand was one of Australia's largest residential land and housing developers with operations in the states of New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria and Western Australia.

Half of the asset base was located in the major population centre of Sydney, with 25 percent in southeast Queensland (the location of Brisbane and the Gold Coast), 15 percent in Melbourne, and 10 percent in Perth.
Funds raised would be used to finance expansion and ensure commercially prudent gearing during the expansion phase, DBS said.
